post_details: I am designing sportswear that includes helmets and need to add stickers and other decoration to the helmet. Is this possible to do with Clo3d? You can see in the image where I am looking to add the same graphic that is on the shoulder. Thanks in advance for any help.

comments.comment_body: Hi 7879035591961 Is the Helmet an OBJ or FBX file? If so you will need to unwrap the texture (Blender can work for this) and add the stickers separately in Photoshop

The helmet is an OBJ file. I understand your solution. I am wondering if there is way to add decals another way? I do so many of these models for sportswear clients that I need a way to do this within CLO, if only just for speed. Is there another model file type that would allow me to add graphics within the program? Is there a way to "sew" a panel onto the helmet then fill that panel with the graphic?

Hi 7879035591961 You could create a pattern piece with fabric that has an Opacity of 0 with the logo added as a graphic. Then add avatar tape to the helmet and use the attach to avatar tool to attached the "invisible" pattern piece with the logo to the helmet
408464537934 Hello! I'm very interested in this, but.... could you be clearer about the process? I don't really understand it! Thank you!
7879035591961 By any chance, have you already tried and succeeded? Regards!

Dear 426926808093, - Create a pattern piece and add the logo as a graphic. Create a fabric for which you set the Opacity to 0 and apply it to the pattern piece. You will now have a pattern piece that is invisible except for the applied graphic. - Add avatar tape to the helmet, see here: https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115012379848-Circumference-Avatar-Tape &amp https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115012380748-Linear-Avatar-Tape - Attach the pattern piece to the helmet via Attach to Avatar Tape: https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115012225987-Attach-to-Avatar-Tape
This process works well enough.

post_title: Making a tuck dart makes program crash!
post_details: I am trying to create a tuck dart and every time I get to where I make the dart length 0 it tells me to edit the point curve and then it crashes. What can I do to fix this?

comments.comment_body: Hi 902924979983, likely the issue occurs because the program gets confused by the command of 0mm, as a dart in CLO is always cut out of the pattern piece (theoretically it's a seam allowance and they are not active parts of a pattern piece inside CLO). If you wish to achieve a tuck dart, you should instead not create a dart but attach it through a custom pleat. Please see a video here that shows how to sew a custom pleat - you can apply the same principle to your tuck dart's position: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BRYTmm-MQi0&ampt=1380s

post_title: 3D Pen Avatar - Copy texture/colour info from imported obj
post_details: I am importing fully uv'd and colour texture mapped .obj's into Clo3d as Avatars and creating patterns for recreating them in fabric/foam using the '3D Pen Avatar' function. What I would really like to do is have the colour/texture info from the Avatar transfer onto my pattern when hitting flatten so each section is appropriately coloured, when reassembled I have a fully printed plushie style object. Is that currently possible?

comments.comment_body: Hi 15369071950489 Currently when using the 3D pen CLO will assign to the default fabric in the Object Browser or whatever fabric is currently selected. There is no way to CLO to read what the avatar looks like and apply that to the fabric/pattern piece. You will need to create your own textures/fabrics and apply them once the pattern pieces are made.
